biggest_gap.what: The piece diagnosed the province's worst authorial habit exactly right — 'a province that only ever says lease has adopted the Provincial Office's vocabulary as narration' — and prescribed exactly the right remedy: 'the euphemism must be somebody's POSITION and not the world's voice'. CF-D008 was then registered with two positions, and BOTH are voiced in dialogue by the coloniser. Position A is an Imperial clerk: 'No subject of the Empire may be held as property inside the Empire's law. Where it happens it happens outside that law, off foreign keels, and the Office has made representations. I've copied three of them myself.' Position B is a House Dres slave-factor: 'The House keeps a stock column and people are entered in it and taken out of it, and the law you are quoting changes the word on the paper and nothing else.' Both books voicing B are Dunmer and Imperial hands — a salt-factor's ledger and marginalia in a borrowed Imperial address. Of 347 people in the province, 227 are Argonian; 66 of those have any answer to the topic `slavery`; between them they give three distinct sentences, and the only one written for an Argonian mouth is untagged and is a refusal to speak: 'This one will not discuss it with you standing there, and this one is sorry.' Carrying no `cf`, it contributes nothing to the 27-of-27 census, nothing to the 43/43 perturbation, and nothing to the register. Meanwhile CF-D008/B's held_by names 'every soul who has been on the Blackrose roll' and its machine holders list `dres-factor, sapcutter, mudborn, outlaw` — of which only dres-factor has a line. The registry credits the enslaved with a position and the build gives them no sentence. And the ruling on this dispute, which the registry's own note calls 'the province's central moral fact', is one of the nine that recover from the shipped bytes in three guesses.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: RI-LOR06 §1.2 forbids the world from correcting a contradiction, and §2 gives held_by one job: to stop a dispute nobody actually holds. Both rules are satisfied on paper and inverted in practice. The register was built to move the euphemism from narration into somebody's mouth; it moved it into two colonists' mouths and left the people it is about exactly where they were, which is silent. That is not a small authorial miss — it is the difference between a province that depicts a colonial vocabulary and a province that has adopted one, and RI-LOR01's 'How we lose' #7 names precisely this failure ('Imperial contempt swallowed whole ... the game must know the difference even when the book does not'). It is also the piece's own thesis failing on its own headline example, which is the strongest possible argument that the register's 0.019% behavioural footprint is a real limit and not a technicality.

remedy.action: Three edits, all in data. (1) Tag the existing Saxhleel refusal in game/data/dialogue/topics/40-race-gated.json with `cf: CF-D008` and a third position C — a refusal to answer an Imperial question in front of an Imperial building is a claim about what is the case, held by the people it is the case about — and register position C with holders drawn from Argonian actors. (2) Write one cf-tagged CF-D008/B line for `mudborn`, `sapcutter` or `outlaw`, actors the registry ALREADY declares hold that position and which no line reaches. (3) Salt the truth_seal (`sha256(id + '|' + ruling + '|' + corpus-side salt)`) so CF-D008's ruling stops recovering in three guesses, and drop the >=24-character guard from both leak checks so the instrument can see the case it is currently blind to.
remedy.acceptance: node tools/lore/critic-w1-23-r1-voices.mjs reports at least one distinct answer to `slavery` that is cf-tagged AND written for an Argonian actor, in addition to the clerk and the dres-factor. For CF-D008, the set of actors that can be OFFERED a cf-tagged line is no longer a subset of {clerk, dres-factor}: at least one of mudborn, sapcutter or outlaw is in it. node tools/lore/critic-w1-23-r1.mjs reports 0 of 26 sealed rulings recoverable (currently 9), and its --self-test still passes 6/6. node tools/lore/canon-census.mjs and node tools/lore/canon-consumption.mjs still PASS, and the untagged-voice count from the critic probe falls from 20 toward 0.

secondary_observations.what: THE CENSUS AND THE CONSUMER MEASURE TWO DIFFERENT POPULATIONS. 20 of the 70 declared dialogue voices point at an info carrying no `cf` tag: the census counts them, resolve() passes them because it checks only that an info exists for that actor, and the register gates nothing there. All of CF-D002, CF-D003, CF-D004 and CF-D005 are in this set — four of the six disputes RI-LOR06 §2 seeds as load-bearing, the ones the world is actually about. canon-census.mjs --self-test has a check for 'a voice attributed to an actor with no info there' and none for 'a voice attributed to an info that makes no claim', which is why it reads 10/10 with 20 live instances on disk. Two lines in the census close it.

THE SIX TRIBES WERE APPENDED, NOT ABSORBED. Ten NPCs across six peoples — Agacephs 2, Paatru 2, Archein 2, Sarpa 1, Miredancers 2, Dead-Water 1 — in a province of 347, with one or two speakers each and no faction record anywhere: game/data/factions/ does not exist and game/data/progression/factions.json lists only house-dres and shadowscale-order. Six disputes were added to the headline while the population able to argue them grew by ten. CF-C023's own condition was 'If tribes are wanted, they need a faction each, not a mention each'; they got a mention each plus a speaker each. The dialogue itself is good and the tribe-census's five-axis differentiation (worst overlap 0 of 5) is real work — the criticism is of scale, not of craft.

WHAT THE REGISTER DOES DO, AND IT IS WORTH KEEPING. Of the 31 answers it changes, several are stanceOf()'s deliberate 'a speaker who matches two positions holds NEITHER' rule catching real authorial collisions: four Wet Ledger clerks match CF-D008 position A by actor and position B by faction, and are therefore given neither, rather than being handed the Provincial Office's denial by an accident of the actor field. That is a genuine correctness property and no other mechanism in the build provides it. It argues for widening the register's reach, not for removing it.

THE SEAL IS STRONGEST WHERE IT MATTERS MOST, WHICH IS WHY THE HOLE IS FIXABLE. All 17 unrecoverable seals are `partial:` rulings, including CF-D001 (what survives in the sap), CF-D005 (the Flu, the item's proof-of-convention) and CF-D007 — the dispute nearest CF-C010, the registry's one late-discoverable secret, whose positions state nothing of it. The design instinct was right and the implementation shipped a three-guess back door on the nine rulings that happen to be a single letter.

TWO PHANTOM PATHS AND A BLIND TRIAGE, ALL INSIDE GATES. game/data/books/manifest.json does not exist and RI-LOR06 method §1 — 'runs in CI, blocks the wave' — invokes it, so the anti-forgery clause ('a contradiction whose sources do not exist is not tracked, it is claimed') has never run. game/data/factions/ does not exist and RI-LOR01 method §4 counts it. And canon-check.py --claims reports `registry touches: 0` over 50 infos that carry explicit CF-Dnnn tags, because it matches keywords and does not read the field this piece invented. Three gates, three instruments that cannot fire.

THE CENSUS STILL IS NOT A GATE, AND THE BUILDER SAID SO. tools/lore/canon-census.mjs exits non-zero and nothing runs it: grep across tools/, .githooks/ and package.json finds one reference, in build-canon.mjs's header prose. check-content.mjs contains the string 'canon' zero times. The builder's stated reason — a hard gate landed mid-wave would fail another builder's in-flight book — was sound at the time and the wave's library work has now landed. Its MAGNITUDE is the finding: 31 of 161,702 answers, all silencings, and the disagreements the report offers as evidence survive the register's deletion unchanged.

corpus_extended.what: Comparison method §4 counts disputes 'whose positions are both actually voiced in shipped content by a real book or NPC'. It does not say that a dialogue voice must be a line the register can gate, and the shipped census therefore accepts a voiced_by naming an info that carries no cf tag. Twenty such voices exist today. Suggested amendment: method §4 should require that every `dialogue:` voice name an info carrying the matching `cf` and `pos`, so that the census's population and the consumer's are the same set.

Check 8 (drift) covers `tier` moves and `authorially_true` changes. It does not cover a `measured:` claim on an undisputed fact being falsified by the shipped tree, which is how CF-C023 went false with every gate green. Suggested amendment: check 8 should re-evaluate any registry field that asserts a count over game/data.

Comparison method §4 counts named factions in `game/data/factions/`, which does not exist in this build; factions live as string ids on NPC records and as two entries in game/data/progression/factions.json. Either the item's path or the build's layout needs to move, and until one does the invention-density axis is unmeasurable and the item scores 0 by min-over-axes.

method_deviations.deviation: Wrote tools/lore/critic-w1-23-r1.mjs, a critic-owned instrument sharing no code with the builder's two tools, covering five questions neither of them asks: seal invertibility, whole-province ablation, voice-versus-gate, reach-versus-speech, and falsified `measured:` claims. It self-tests all five in both directions and exits non-zero only when a finding is present.
method_deviations.why: RULES #4 and #6. The piece's own instruments are green and well made; a critic that re-runs them has measured nothing. The ablation in particular is the delete-the-fix the piece did not run, and RULES #6's second clause ('then check the two arms actually differ') is exactly what it answers.

method_deviations.deviation: Did not run comparison method §5 (x-density and long-vowel coverage over Jel-classified names) or §6 (blind culture-attribution).
method_deviations.why: §§1-2's harvester feeds §5 its Jel-classified set and that set is 616 'names' of which 552 violate, most of them sentences. §5 computed over that set would be a statistic about book titles. §6 requires a fresh judge and no fresh-judge channel exists to a critic in this harness (the same constraint the W1-LIBRARY round-1 verdict recorded). Both are recorded not-run rather than passed.

method_deviations.deviation: No browser was used and no engine-level boot measurement was taken; the consumption evidence comes from importing game/src/world/canon.js and game/src/character/converse.js directly in node.
method_deviations.why: RULES #21 — 18 headless_shell were live at loadavg 9.99 when this run began, above the ~8 threshold, and contention has cost two pieces their headline numbers. Every figure in this verdict is a count or a boolean, which survive contention; none is a timing. The engine-level half (that _installCanon runs at boot and throws) is verified by reading engine.js:2269-2281 and by the fail-closed arms of resolve(), not by observing a boot, and that limit is stated here rather than papered over.

arbitration_questions.question: CF-C023 is a W1-23 registration that the tribes piece falsified without updating. Which piece owns the failure: the registry that wrote a dated measurement into a binding constructed fact, or the piece that changed the tree under it? I have scored it against W1-23 as a check fail rather than an item-level 0, on the ground that the gap it exposes — a census that cannot see a falsified `measured:` claim — is W1-23's instrument, not the tribes piece's content.

Every number was re-derived by a tool sharing no code with the builder's, and where mine overlap the builder's they agree — 141 references, 409 untagged controls, the 27-of-27 census — which is the reason I trust the ones that disagree.
